name: Sclerosteosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Sclerosteosis

criteria.description: Progressive generalized cortical bone overgrowth primarily affecting the skull and long bones
Syndactyly of fingers or toes, typically involving the second and third digits
Recurrent or progressive facial nerve palsy due to cranial nerve entrapment
Radiographic evidence of skull bone thickening and sclerosis
Identification of loss-of-function mutations in the SOST gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive bone overgrowth with syndactyly plus radiographic skull thickening; genetic confirmation supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing can confirm but is not always available.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Skull bone thickening with facial distortion

common.symptomName: Facial nerve palsy due to cranial nerve entrapment
Hearing loss secondary to cranial nerve compression
Visual impairment due to optic nerve compression

rare.symptomName: Seizures secondary to increased intracranial pressure
Respiratory compromise due to skull base overgrowth

imaging: Skull X-ray showing cortical thickening and sclerosis
CT/MRI demonstrating skull base hyperostosis and cranial nerve compression
Radiographs of long bones showing cortical hyperostosis
genetic: Loss-of-function mutations in the SOST gene (encoding sclerostin)

distinguishingFeatures: Similar bone overgrowth but absence of syndactyly
More severe craniofacial hyperostosis with facial disfigurement
Presence of anemia and other hematological abnormalities

references: Brunkow ME, et al. Bone dysplasia sclerosteosis results from loss of the SOST gene product, a novel cystine knot-containing protein. Am J Hum Genet. 2001.
Balemans W, et al. Increased bone density in sclerosteosis is due to the deficiency of a novel secreted protein (SOST). Hum Mol Genet. 2001.
